proofs.full_local_argument: Choose h>0 so x+(delta+3h)B_d⊂U; compactness and openness allow this. On a neighborhood of this compact set, f is continuous and uniformly continuous. Smooth mollifications f_epsilon=f*rho_epsilon are therefore defined on x+(delta+2h)B_d for sufficiently small epsilon and converge uniformly there to f. For ||z−x||<h put F_epsilon(z)=vol(delta B_d)^{-1} integral_{delta B_d} f_epsilon(z+w)dw. Differentiation and the divergence theorem, applied separately to each coordinate, give ∇F_epsilon(z)=vol(delta B_d)^{-1} integral_{delta sphere} f_epsilon(z+w)(w/delta)dA(w)=(d/delta)E_u[f_epsilon(z+delta u)u]. In dimension one the same formula follows by differentiating (2delta)^{-1}integral_{−delta}^{delta} f_epsilon(z+w)dw, giving [f_epsilon(z+delta)−f_epsilon(z−delta)]/(2delta). Uniform convergence on the larger compact ball implies uniform convergence F_epsilon→F and ∇F_epsilon→H on ||z−x||≤h/2, where H(z)=(d/delta)E_u[f(z+delta u)u]. H is continuous by uniform continuity of f. For z and z+k in this smaller ball with the connecting segment inside it, the smooth fundamental theorem gives F_epsilon(z+k)−F_epsilon(z)=integral_0^1 ∇F_epsilon(z+tk)·k dt. Passing to the uniform limit gives the same equality with F and H. Hence |F(z+k)−F(z)−H(z)·k|≤||k|| sup_{0≤t≤1}||H(z+tk)−H(z)||=o(||k||). Thus F is differentiable with continuous gradient H, proving the assertion at x. Every integration used is finite on the compact neighborhood. This is a complete local argument, not a claim that the source explicitly proved this regularity completion.

assumptions: The closed ball x+delta B_d has an open neighborhood U on which f is locally Lipschitz.
This is the seed's explicit sufficient-regularity subcase; the source does not print this regularity condition and its phrase for any function is not adopted without qualification.
statement.conclusion: ∇F(x)=(d/delta) E_u[f(x+delta u)u]. Consequently the vector (d/delta)f(x+delta u)u has mean ∇F(x).
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let B_d={v∈R^d:||v||_2≤1}. Let f:U→R be locally Lipschitz on an open set U containing x+delta B_d. Define F(z)=E_{v uniform on B_d}f(z+delta v) wherever z+delta B_d⊂U, and sample u uniformly on the unit sphere; for d=1 this is uniform on {-1,1}.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every integer d≥1, every delta>0, every such f and every x with the stated neighborhood, F is continuously differentiable locally at x and the identity holds. Expectations are integration identities, not oracle-noise assumptions.

title: Ball smoothing gradient identity: locally Lipschitz subcase
use_when: Check the conditional mean of a sphere-sampled one-value estimator; distinguish the ball smoothing distribution from the sphere sampling distribution.
